intended_object: Hölder continuity with constant C and exponent r of a map between (pseudo-extended) metric spaces: d(f x, f y) ≤ C·d(x,y)^r for all x, y (from the docstring and name).
explanation: The body states exactly the Hölder inequality for all pairs of points, using extended distances in ℝ≥0∞ and a real power. It is stated in the most general setting, pseudo-extended-metric spaces, with a nonnegative constant and exponent, which is the standard convention. The edge cases behave correctly under the ℝ≥0∞ conventions: 0^0 = 1, so exponent 0 means oscillation bounded by C; 0·∞ = 0, so C = 0 forces f to be constant up to distance zero; for r > 0, pairs at infinite distance impose no constraint (when C > 0). This is Mathlib's own definition, and Mathlib has no more general one.
